hardcoded-private-key.title: Private key material embedded in source
hardcoded-private-key.why: A private key checked into a repository is compromised the moment anyone clones, forks or mirrors it, and rotating it means re-issuing every signature, certificate or account that depends on it. Git keeps the value in history even after the line is deleted, so removal is never enough on its own. Keys belong in a KMS, an HSM or (at minimum) an environment variable injected at deploy time.

key-file-outside-tests.title: Key file stored outside test/fixture directories
key-file-outside-tests.why: A `.pem`, `.key`, `id_ecdsa` or `.p12` file that sits next to application code is almost always a real key that was committed by accident — throwaway keys normally live under `test/`, `fixtures/` or `examples/`. Anyone with read access to the repository, including CI logs and forks, gets the key. If the file really is a disposable fixture, move it into a test directory so the intent is obvious to both humans and scanners.
key-file-outside-tests.fix:
# keep keys out of the tree
git rm --cached path/to/private.key
echo '*.key' >> .gitignore
# then rotate the key — a committed key must be considered public

findings.title: Private key material embedded in source
findings.message: A private key block (`-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`) is embedded in source. Treat this key as compromised: rotate it, then remove the value from git history.
